'''Amenohiwake-no-Mikoto''' (''amenohiwake no mikoto''; dates of birth and death unknown) was a {{ill|gōzoku|ja|豪族}} of ancient {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}} and the first '''{{ill|Ise no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊勢国造}}'''.

== Overview ==
According to a fragment of the ''Ise no Kuni Fudoki'', he accompanied {{ill|Emperor Jimmu's eastern expedition|ja|神武東征}}, reaching Kumano-mura in {{ill|Kii Province|ja|紀伊国}}, and was further guided by the {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|金烏|lt=Golden Crow}} (Kinshi) to Uda-no-Shimoagata. At that time {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}} commanded {{ill|Ōtomo-no-Hibi-no-Mikoto|ja|道臣命|lt=Ōtomo-no-Hibi-no-Mikoto|lt_ja=大伴日臣命}} to swiftly subjugate {{ill|Nagasunehiko|ja|長髄彦}}, and likewise commanded Amenohiwake-no-Mikoto: "There is a land in the direction of heaven. Pacify that land," and granted him a marker-sword (''shime-no-tsurugi'').

Amenohiwake-no-Mikoto obeyed the command and reached a settlement several hundred ''ri'' to the east, where there was a deity named {{ill|Isetsuhiko|ja|伊勢津彦}}. Amenohiwake asked, "Will you give your land to the Heavenly Grandchild?" Isetsuhiko replied, "I have long sought and dwelt in this land; I dare not heed your command." Amenohiwake raised troops to kill him; Isetsuhiko, afraid, said, "I will give the land entirely to the Heavenly Grandchild. I dare not remain." When Amenohiwake demanded a sign of his departure, Isetsuhiko answered, "This night I will raise the eight winds and stir up the sea, ride the waves, and enter the east. That will be the proof of my retreat." Amenohiwake-no-Mikoto arrayed his troops and watched: in the night a great wind arose, the waves rose up shining like the {{ill|sun|ja|太陽}} so that land and sea alike were illuminated, and Isetsuhiko departed eastward on the waves. When Amenohiwake-no-Mikoto reported the pacification, Emperor Jimmu rejoiced greatly and declared, "Let the land take the name of its earth-deity (Isetsuhiko) and be called Ise." He also granted Amenohiwake-no-Mikoto residence at Miminashi-mura in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国|lt=Ō-Yamato Province|lt_ja=大倭国}}.

The fragment of the ''Ise no Kuni Fudoki'' places Amenohiwake-no-Mikoto as a twelfth-generation descendant of {{ill|Amenominakanushi-no-Mikoto|ja|天御中主尊}}; the {{ill|Ise Ason|ja|伊勢氏|lt=Ise-no-Ason}} entry of the Sakyō Shinbetsu of the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}}'' records his genealogy as grandson of Amenosokotachi-no-Mikoto. Take-Ikataki-no-Mikoto, named in the ''{{ill|Kōtai Jingū Gishikichō|ja|皇太神宮儀式帳}}'' and other sources, is said in the ''Ise Nisho Daijingū Shinmei Hisho'' to be a fifth-generation descendant of Amenohiwake-no-Mikoto.

Nakatomi Shrine, the {{ill|shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} merged into {{ill|Kuwana-Sōsha|ja|桑名宗社}}, enshrines Amenohiwake-no-Mikoto as its deity.
